name: MAIN STREET
note: Room 2. The hub, and the most-visited screen in the game. LOOK and LISTEN lines are verbatim from docs/05-examine-layer.md; repeat variants and verb overrides are verbatim from docs/13-room-02-content.md; the four exits from docs/14-room-02-exits.md. Nothing on this screen was written by anyone implementing it.

ordinary.note: Claims, disputes, and one advertisement for a patent hernia truss.

funeral.note: Act III. The clean white sheet is Thad's own funeral notice -- 'Frame has finally found a spelling he cannot get wrong.' Set by doc 48's S2.

LOOK_AT.say: My funeral notice, prominently posted. 'THE PIANO MAN, MOURNED BY ALL.' Frame has finally found a spelling he can't get wrong.
Claims for sale, claims disputed, maps to Mott's strike. I've met Mott. He'd have bought a map.
Claims for sale, claims disputed, a lost dog, and a man offering to write letters home for those who can't. He's doing better than anyone.
repeat: The lost dog notice has been up six weeks. The dog is on this street.
Four claims for sale today. There were three yesterday.

LISTEN_TO.say: Paper in wind. One of those sheets is my whole official existence, flapping.
Paper in wind, every sheet rustling about one man. He's heard it for twelve years.
Paper, in wind. A great deal of it.
repeat: Paper. Still a great deal of it.
One corner has come loose and is knocking. It'll do that until somebody dies.

overrides.PICK_UP: They belong to the town. I've read them four times, which I consider a form of ownership.
overrides.OPEN: They're already facing out. That's the whole design.

LOOK_AT.say: My reflection, in three inches of water. For a dead man, I look surprisingly worried.
A trough. Three inches of water and a great deal of ambition.
repeat: The water hasn't improved. Neither has my opinion of it.
Three inches. I measured it with a stick. The most scientific thing anyone's done in Consolation this year.

LISTEN_TO.say: Something's still living in it. So am I, whatever the paper says.
Something is living in it. I've decided not to pursue this.
repeat: It's still in there. It's moved.
We have reached an understanding.

overrides.USE: I've drunk from it once. The “once” is doing a great deal of work in that sentence.
overrides.OPEN: It's a trough. It's entirely open. It's nothing but open.

LOOK_AT.say: The dog. He was here before the rumor, and he'll be here after it. I'd like to know his secret.
A dog with the settled look of an animal that has outlasted several owners.
repeat: He hasn't moved. He has the air of a creature waiting for the town to finish.
He's looking at me. I've got nothing to offer, and he knows it.

LISTEN_TO.say: He knows me. Tail, twice. The one resident who's never read a newspaper, so the one resident I'm still alive to.
Breathing. Contented. He's the only solvent resident of Consolation.
repeat: Still contented. Still solvent.
Quiet. He's gone to sleep in the middle of my attention.

overrides.PICK_UP: I'm not picking up a dog I haven't been introduced to.

LOOK_AT.say: The tallest thing in Consolation, and the only building that is as deep as it is tall.
repeat: Still the only honest building on the horizon.
Somebody built that properly. I'd like to meet them. I suspect they've left.

LISTEN_TO.say: The bell is a half-step flat.
repeat: Half a step. Every time.
I've started hearing it in tune, in my head, before it rings. That's the first sign of something.
then: A man has rung it by hand for six years, and he doesn't care.

overrides.PICK_UP: It's four hundred yards away and about forty feet tall. I admire the ambition.
overrides.TALK_TO: I'm not going to shout at a church from the street. I was raised better than that. Slightly.
overrides.USE: It's a steeple. Its use is being seen from everywhere, and it's already doing that.

weathered.note: The plate as generated. Peeling gilt, and the only twice-painted sign in town.

gilt.note: Act III. Doc 05 Part Two-B: 'Fresh gilt on the lettering. Business is good. Business, for the Company, is always the search, and the search just outlived its most annoying obstacle. Me.' Set by doc 48's S2, the funeral, because errata 60 writes ACT at four places and this is one of them.

LOOK_AT.say: Fresh gilt on the lettering. Business is good. The Company's business is the search, and the search has just outlived its most annoying obstacle. Me.
CONSOLATION IMPROVEMENT COMPANY. Two coats of gilt on a rumor. I've met the man who started it. He'd have stopped at one coat.
CONSOLATION IMPROVEMENT COMPANY. Gilt lettering.
repeat: Gilt. Actual gilt. In a town where the road is a suggestion.
Painted twice, and the second time by a better man than the first.
then: The only sign in town that's been painted twice.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. It's the quietest building on the street, and it's always full.
repeat: Still quiet. Still full.
Whatever they do in there, they do it without raising their voices.

overrides.PULL: It's screwed on. Thoroughly. Somebody paid extra for it to stay put.
overrides.TALK_TO: I'm not going to talk to the sign. I'll talk to the man inside, when he'll see me.

LOOK_AT.say: Six inches above the mud. People still step aside for me, then remember I'm dead, and look embarrassed.
Six inches above the mud.
repeat: Six inches. I've never been so aware of six inches.
The boards are good. Somebody spent money on the one thing that keeps a man out of the road.
then: In Consolation, this is the difference between a gentleman and a prospector.

LISTEN_TO.say: Loose board, third from the end. Everyone in town steps over it without thinking.
repeat: Third from the end. Still loose.
It has a note. B flat, roughly. I've decided not to tell anyone.

overrides.PULL: The loose board declines to come up. It is loose recreationally, not professionally.
overrides.PUSH: Third from the end. Up an inch, down an inch. I did that four more times than I needed to.

LOOK_AT.say: Every pick in those hills is still looking for Mott's strike. Nobody's looking for me. I find I mind.
Every pick in those hills is after Mott's strike. Mott never struck anything. They all look so busy.
Gold country. Everyone here has looked at these hills for years and seen a number.
repeat: Still gold country. Still no gold.
The same hills as yesterday. I check.

LISTEN_TO.say: Picks, far off. Honest work, every stroke of it, on a story.
Nothing. They're extremely large, and they aren't doing anything.
repeat: Still large. Still quiet.
Nothing. I'd be alarmed if there were.

overrides.USE: I wouldn't know where to begin, and neither would they.

LOOK_AT.say: The mud. The one thing on this street that treats me exactly as it did before I died.
Mud, the full width of the street and six inches deep.
repeat: The same mud. I've started to recognize individual portions of it.
That portion there, I've named. I won't be sharing the name.
then: The boardwalk is six inches high. Somebody worked that out.

LISTEN_TO.say: Not a sound. The mud sent no flowers.
Nothing. It's mud, being mud.
repeat: Nothing new.
Nothing new. I want that understood.

overrides.PICK_UP: I pick up some mud. I am now a man holding mud, in a street, at night. I put it back.

LOOK_AT.say: Two stories in front, one behind, same as ever — but now every doorway says good morning to me by name. Approximately by name.
Same false fronts. Last week every doorway said good morning to me. This week they're terribly sorry for my loss.
Two stories in front, one behind. I used to call these the town's lie. I've since met the town's lie. These are just carpentry.
Half this street is two stories tall in front and one story deep.
repeat: Still two stories of front and nothing behind. I keep hoping the back will turn up.
I've counted. Six fronts, six sheds, one town.
then: Consolation is a stage set people have moved into.

LISTEN_TO.say: Wind behind them, and under it, my own name being discussed. Approximately my name.
Wind, and two men agreeing I was a fine fellow. Neither one ever met me. I'm touched.
Wind behind them, and nothing else. They never pretended otherwise.
Wind. There's a great deal of nothing behind half of these.
repeat: The same nothing. It's a very consistent nothing.
Nothing. I've stopped expecting otherwise, and I'm the better for it.

overrides.PUSH: I push the front of a building. It doesn't fall over. I'm honestly a little surprised.
overrides.PULL: If I pull hard enough, the whole town comes down. I haven't decided how I feel about that.
overrides.OPEN: The front is the part that doesn't open. That is its entire function and its entire biography.

LOOK_AT.say: The Bountiful Nugget. Batwing doors, which swing both ways. I suspect that's the whole philosophy of the place.
repeat: Somebody spent money on those doors and nothing else. I've looked.
The Nugget. It's bountiful the way a promise is bountiful.

LISTEN_TO.say: Talk, glasses, and a piano that's flat in one place. I could put it right in four minutes, and nobody's asked me.
repeat: Still flat. C-sharp. It's going to be C-sharp for the rest of my life.
Somebody in there is telling a story about a bear. The bear is bigger than it was.

overrides.CLOSE: They swing. Closing them is a temporary opinion.
overrides.TALK_TO: I'd have to go in. Going in costs money.
overrides.PULL: They swing outward, inward, and for some time afterwards.

LOOK_AT.say: CONSOLATION IMPROVEMENT COMPANY. The door is a great deal heavier than the building needs.
repeat: Everyone who goes in comes out pleased. I've watched eleven men do it. I'd like to be the twelfth.
Three stories from here. I've been round the back. It's one.

LISTEN_TO.say: Not a sound. The quietest doorway on the street, and it's never still.
repeat: Not a sound, and somebody is always going in.
Nothing at all. I've never once heard a raised voice through that door.

overrides.PUSH: It opens inward, which is a decision somebody made.
overrides.TALK_TO: Talking to the door won't get me in. The men who go in come out holding maps.
overrides.CLOSE: It closes on its own, slowly, and without a sound. Somebody paid for that too.

LOOK_AT.say: The Consolation Clarion. One press, one man, and the front page of every issue for twelve years has been about a hole nobody can find.
repeat: The door's open. The door's always open. He's desperate for somebody to say something quotable.
There's a bill in the window advertising the Clarion, printed by the Clarion, on the Clarion's press.

LISTEN_TO.say: The press. It knocks on the return stroke. It's knocked for years.
repeat: Knocking. Still knocking.
He's talking to himself in there. Both sides of an interview. He's winning.

overrides.TALK_TO: If I say anything within forty feet of that door, it'll be in print by four o'clock. Spelled wrong.
overrides.CLOSE: He'd only open it again, and then write about it.

LOOK_AT.say: The road out to the diggings. Worn a foot deep by boots — which is more dirt than anybody out there has shifted on purpose.
repeat: Two miles. It looks further in the morning and considerably further at night.
Somewhere down there is forty feet of mud for any man fool enough to buy it.

LISTEN_TO.say: Boots. A great many of them, going out. The most cheerful sound in Consolation, and it happens at six in the morning.
repeat: Nothing at the moment. They're all out there.
Nothing coming back yet. They come back quiet.

overrides.PICK_UP: It's a road. It's two miles long. No.
overrides.PULL: It's a road. It's been pulled about enough.
overrides.CLOSE: I've considered it. Several of us have.

exits.name: THE ASSAY OFFICE
exits.note: Doc 20's graph: the sixth enterable facade. Room 5 was composed, wired with sixteen lines and audited three times while nothing on Main Street opened onto it. Marked stub because doc 05's Room 2 does not script this door and its examine lines are not written; inventing them would be worse than the honest gap. The rect is the door and its step. The lot was drawn BOARDED with tools leaning across it, which is ruling 19b in the other direction -- art asserting a building this exit contradicts -- and it now has a door, clean glass and a worn step, and nothing else. It is still the plainest front on the street.

LOOK_AT.say: The assay office. A door, a step, and one window. The only front on this street that isn't selling itself.
repeat: No sign. Everybody knows where it is and nobody needs telling twice.
The step is worn pale in the middle and nowhere else. They come, they stand, they go.

LISTEN_TO.say: Hardly a sound. Somebody in there is working, and doing it quietly.
repeat: Nothing. A pen, possibly. I may be inventing the pen.
Whatever's decided in there is decided without discussion.

shut.note: As the room composes. Winnie's door is shut because Winnie is working.

open.note:
Doc 22 item 9, and the appearance change that does NOT change identity: it is still THE ASSAY OFFICE, so it is one object with two states rather than the coach's two hotspots with opposite gates. The bounds widen by the swung leaf, which is why per-state bounds exist -- hit-testing the shut door's rect after it opens is the kind of wrongness nobody reports because it nearly works.

THE LEAF IS NOT DRAWN, AND THE BOUNDS ARE THE DOOR'S OWN (2026-09-05, Room 5's Act I pass). The open state used to carry `room-02-assay-door-open.png` -- a 320x144 overlay cut from the composed facade errata 54 discarded (doc 36 Q20's void table) -- and bounds in that space, [1752,300,120,192]. Drawn, the overlay stretched across the whole 3700px plate as a smear beside the hotel; hit-tested, the bounds put the door in the middle of the road, so after the first pass through it the door could not be clicked where it is drawn and Room 5 could not be re-entered from the street. The state still turns on transit (the probe reports it), so the appearance change has a place to land when a leaf exists at plate scale; until then the door looks shut and works. Authoring that leaf is an art operation Tyler authorizes, not a fix.

overrides.PUSH: It opens inward, and easily. Somebody oils it.
overrides.CLOSE: It closes itself, slowly, and latches. Somebody sees to that.
overrides.TALK_TO: I've tried talking to it. The building isn't the problem.

exits.name: THE HOTEL
exits.note: Doc 20: the hotel is one of the six facades. Stub until doc 14 covers it, as it did not cover the assay office until Room 5 was written.

exits.name: THE MERCANTILE
exits.note: Doc 20: one of Main Street's six façades, the store with goods in its window west of the Company. It had no door until Room 12 was built (errata 85 E). Doc 14 writes no lines for it, so it carries none (doc 36 Q155).

exits.name: THE BACK LOTS
exits.note: Doc 20: 'East, the back lots | 20 · back alley' -- the street's east end, past the mercantile. NO DOCUMENT WRITES THIS WAY a LOOK or LISTEN. A stub exit (doc 36 Q163, errata 93 C).

walkBoxes.note: ERRATA 28a: fixed at the far drawn size, and that is where Room 2's scaling snap now lives. The boardwalk lip is the only real horizontal interruption in the walkable band -- measured at a mean luminance step of 64.5 against 16.3 for the next strongest row -- so stepping off it into the mud is where the sprite swaps from the drawn far sheet to a decimated one. Before boxes the height was one curve across the whole floor and the swap landed at y109, in open mud.

occlusionPlanes.note: The near corner alone -- the lumber stack and the wagon wheel. An actor in the near mud is masked by this and by nothing else, so he passes BEHIND the woodpile and IN FRONT of the trough, which is the point of having two planes rather than one flat overlay.
occlusionPlanes.maskPendingIssue: docs/36-issue-list.md::Q20 · BOTH OF MAIN STREET'S OCCLUSION MASKS DESCRIBE A STREET THAT NO LONGER EXISTS
occlusionPlanes.maskPendingNote:
THE MASK DOES NOT DESCRIBE THIS PLATE. Found by rendering it over the background and looking, which is the only way it could have been found: the shapes are well-formed, they sit in plausible places, and every geometric test passes on them -- check-occlusion measures 31% of the drawn figure covered at the proof point below, which is a real overlap with a shape that is not in the picture.

MEASURED. The mask is 320x144 -- errata 54's voided presentation, doc 36 Q17 -- and `Renderer.masked` stretches it to the room's 3700x864, which is a defined behaviour and not the same as authoring it at room resolution. Stretched, plane 1 draws a WAGON WHEEL with eight spokes and a slab beside it across x0-940 of the near mud. The plate there is open mud: no wheel, no lumber, nothing. Panel C of the room proof shows a man standing in the middle of it, drawn whole, with nothing to be behind.

I GOT THIS WRONG ONCE AND THE WAY I GOT IT WRONG IS THE WARNING. Reading the overlay, I took the wheel the MASK draws for a wheel in the PLATE and recorded that plane 1 'traces the wheel's spokes exactly'. It traces its own. A mask rendered over a background looks like a highlighted object whether or not there is an object there, and only turning the mask off answers it.

WHILE THIS IS TRUE THE RENDERER SKIPS THE PLANE and draws straight through -- which is what it did anyway when every box said clipPlane 12, so nothing regresses. Regenerating both masks at 3700x864 against the current plate is art, and Tyler's.

occlusionPlanes.note: Plane 1 plus the hitching rail and the water trough. CONTAINS plane 1 on purpose: doc 22 section 5 says an actor is masked by its own plane and not by a union of every plane, so each level has to carry everything nearer than the actors assigned to it. An actor in the middle band or further is behind all of it.
occlusionPlanes.maskPendingIssue: docs/36-issue-list.md::Q20 · BOTH OF MAIN STREET'S OCCLUSION MASKS DESCRIBE A STREET THAT NO LONGER EXISTS
occlusionPlanes.maskPendingNote:
THE MASK IS STALE AND DOES NOT DESCRIBE THIS PLATE. Found by rendering it over the background and looking, which is the only way it could have been found: the shapes are well-formed, they are in plausible places, and every geometric test passes on them.

MEASURED. The mask is 320x144 -- errata 54's voided presentation, doc 36 Q17 -- and `Renderer.masked` stretches it to the room's 3700x864, which is a defined behaviour and not the same as authoring it at room resolution. Stretched, plane 2 adds two regions beyond plane 1's corner: x1110-1640 in the middle band, which is a HITCHING RAIL, two posts and a crossbar, drawn precisely -- and there is no hitching rail in the plate there; and x2480-2930, a plain rectangle over open mud in front of the saloon. Neither touches the water trough at x1862-2017 y543-605, which this plane's own note says it contains. It was authored against an earlier, narrower Main Street.

PLANE 1 IS PENDING FOR THE SAME REASON, and was nearly not: its mask draws a wagon wheel over what is open mud in the current plate, and the wheel looked like the plate's until the mask was turned off. Both masks are stale together.

WHILE THIS IS TRUE THE RENDERER SKIPS THE PLANE and draws straight through -- which is what it did anyway when every box said clipPlane 12, so nothing regresses. Activating a stale mask would be worse than the inert state it replaces: an actor in the middle of the street would be erased from the knees down by a rail that is not drawn. Regenerating it at 3700x864 against the current plate is art, and Tyler's.

occlusionNote: No box in this room is clipPlane 0. Doc 22 defines 0 as always-in-front and nothing in Main Street is nearer than the wagon wheel, whose base sits on the bottom row of the frame -- so there is no depth for such a box to occupy. Recorded rather than left to look like an oversight.

atmosphere.note: ERRATA 33b. Rows 0-20 only: the false fronts reach into the top third, so measuring 'above the horizon' would grade the facades against themselves.
atmosphere.skylineNote: The terrace, the ridges and the steeple -- everything that meets the sky. The mud below the boardwalk is ground, not skyline.

onEnter.note: His first sight of the town, and the words come from doc 05's THE FALSE FRONTS rather than being written fresh -- he has the opinion already; this is him having it out loud at the moment he first has it. AMENDED AFTER TYLER CHECKED IT AGAINST THE PLATE: the original said EVERY building was a false front, which the picture contradicts -- the saloon is a flat parapet with a low roof behind it, and the hotel beside it is genuinely two storeys with lit windows and real depth. The plate is signed off, so the writing yields, and the observation is better for it: the half that is real is the half with money, which is the town's whole economy in one line. Gated on T_SEEN_MAIN_STREET, which onEnter sets, so it plays once.
say: Half of it is two stories tall in front and one story deep.
The other half is real, and is doing better.

accost.note: Doc 57 F4 and doc 03: Fanshawe calls the duel himself, 'to discredit Thad in front of the whole town before Thad can be heard'. His challenge and the first boast are the greeting; the duel is running when the counters are offered.

occlusionProofs.note: In the near mud where plane 1's mask, stretched to the room, covers x0-940 across the whole band. GEOMETRICALLY SOUND AND VISUALLY WRONG, which is why the plane is marked maskPending: what the mask draws there is a wagon wheel and the plate underneath is open mud. Kept, not deleted -- the day the mask is regenerated against this plate, the near band's proof point is already standing and the assertion goes live with it.
